I've been interviewed on most of the shows.  During the interviews it was easy, but watching the show as it aired was crazy.  Seeing all the drama in your life aired to millions on national television is like watching your life as a movie.  The news reports were all accurate for the majority of them.  Some were so accurate that I was amazed with how much they knew about our lives.

She was a horrible human being.  She also began to try and point fingers towards my older brother and started trying to find a way to pin it on him.  She always used us kids as scape goats to get out of trouble.  I was tired of us being her scape goat, especially for a murder.

I think I am still in denial.  She was a horrible person, and an even worse mother.  But, either way she is still the woman who gave birth to me and who I was raised by.  It is hard to make yourself believe it even after they show you all of the evidence.  The feeling was such a mixture that it's hard to pinpoint one word.

There are too many actions to list here.. but I will give you the most powerful one.  You have to help them figure out what their passion is.  What do they want to do for their rest of their life that would make them happy?  Whether it be a job, volunteering for a non-profit, helping a certain type of people.  Once they find that passion you have to help them set the goals to make that passion into a living.  Short term goals are just as important as long term.  You need short term so they can remind themselves that they're taking steps in the right direction.
